title: The Lexicon
subtitle: Twenty-four stones. Eighteen point twenty carats. No two cuts identical. The round brilliant: the most spoken diamond dialect in history — light calculated, faceted, perfected over a century of cutting science. The oval: the round's more elegant sibling, elongating the wrist, softening every room it enters. The pear: tension in silhouette — pointed at one end, yielding at the other. The cut that holds contradiction and makes it beautiful. The emerald: architecture. Still. Direct. The only cut that asks you to look into it, not just at it. The cushion: warmth encoded in geometry — softened corners that carry depth most shapes cannot. Together, they form a sentence. Twenty-four words. One unbroken thought, worn on the wrist.
